newsitem.title: USA: Hough says Florida campaign donation was returned.
newsitem.headline: Hough says Florida campaign donation was returned.

text.p: The $240 campaign contribution that cost William R Hough & Co a Pinellas County, Fla., bond deal was made inadvertantly and has been returned, senior vice president Helen Feinberg said Tuesday.

The firm voluntarily withdrew as senior manager for last week's $50 million Pinellas County Housing Authority bond issue after discovering an employee had donated $480 to a county commissioner's election campaign.
Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board rule G-37 bars municipal bond firms from doing business with an issuer for two years if firm members make campaign donations exceeding $250 to issuer officials.
Feinberg said the employee who made the donation had intended to give $240, which is below the limit that triggers the rule, but that the contribution was accidentally duplicated.

"Due to the fact that it was an inadvertant second $240 contribution, that was immediately discovered with our internal policies and procedures," Feinberg said. "The contribution was also immediately returned. In terms of out-of-pocket dollars and value received by the campaign, we are under that (limit)."
She said Hough voluntarily consulted the National Association of Securities Dealers and requested a waiver from the two- year rule, but was denied and is appealing.
"We are seeking relief from the two-year ban," Feinberg said.
